strengths: The paper addresses an important and emerging problem: extending time-series foundation models to support multimodal inputs (text and image) to enhance cross-domain generalization.

The proposed Prototype-Guided Flow Matching is an interesting attempt to introduce domain-specific priors (trend and periodicity prototypes) as the starting point of the generative flow instead of pure Gaussian noise.

The evaluation is extensive, spanning multiple scenarios (multimodal zero-shot/few-shot, unimodal zero-shot deterministic, and unimodal zero-shot probabilistic) across well-recognized benchmarks (TimeMMD, TSFM-Bench, and ProbTS) with a large suite of baseline models.
weaknesses: Lack of architectural novelty: The architecture is largely a combination of existing techniques. The conversion of time series to 2D images via FFT and rendering is directly adopted from VisionTS (Chen et al., 2024a). The token distillation mechanism is a standard cross-attention compression module (similar to Perceiver/Q-Former), and the text/vision encoders rely on off-the-shelf BERT and ViT models.

Heuristically designed Modality-Guided Self-Attention: In Equation 14, the cross-modality correlation matrix is defined as $Corr = VAttn \cdot W \cdot TAttn^T$. $VAttn$ and $TAttn$ represent how the time series tokens correlate with visual and textual distilled tokens, respectively. Multiplying these two attention maps via a learnable matrix $W$ to inject back as temporal self-attention bias (Equation 16) lacks a rigorous theoretical justification. It is unclear why the product of cross-modal relationships should represent or correct the raw temporal self-correlation of the time series.

Extreme computational overhead: As shown in Table 8, Aurora is highly resource-intensive. It has the highest MACs (18.329 G) and the longest inference latency (83.5 ms) among almost all baselines, including massive models like Time-MoE. The high latency and complexity undermine its practicality as an out-of-the-box, real-time forecaster.

Lack of qualitative analysis and visualization: The central claim is that text and visual modalities guide future trends and periodicities via the Prototype Bank and Modality-Guided Attention. However, the paper lacks any visual analysis or case studies showing what these prototypes actually represent, how the text/images map to them, or how the cross-modal attention matrices behave.

Over-reliance on extremely concurrent/future preprints: The bibliography and text are heavily saturated with citations dated 2025 (e.g., Qiu et al., 2025d, Wu et al., 2025a, Wang et al., 2025c, Liu et al., 2025a, Li et al., 2025d). While keeping up with the literature is good, relying heavily on unpublished or highly concurrent preprints as foundational baselines makes the positioning of the paper unstable.

strengths: The paper introduces a novel and timely topic: a multimodal generative time series foundation model that supports zero-shot inference and incorporates domain knowledge from text and visual representations.

The proposed architecture is well-designed. In particular, the Modality-Guided Multi-head Self-Attention mechanism effectively fuses multimodal features, and the Prototype-Guided Flow Matching successfully leverages periodic/trend priors (trigonometric, polynomial bases) to guide generative trajectories rather than starting from standard Gaussian noise.

The evaluation is highly comprehensive, covering both multimodal (TimeMMD) and unimodal (TSFM-Bench, ProbTS) scenarios, deterministic and probabilistic forecasting, and showing consistent improvements over strong baselines like Sundial, MOIRAI, Chronos, and CALF.
The ablation studies are detailed and clearly validate the contribution of each proposed component (Modality-Guided Attention and Prototype-Guided Flow Matching).
weaknesses: A major concern lies in the realism and source of the multimodal data. The textual descriptions in the pretraining dataset are synthetically generated by GPT-4 using the raw time series data itself, and the images are 2D rendered directly from the 1D time series. Thus, these modalities do not bring genuine exogenous multimodal information, but rather act as alternative hand-crafted/automated representations of the unimodal time series. The paper should discuss this limitation and the practical availability of text descriptions in real-world scenarios.

Inference complexity is high. As shown in Table 8, Aurora has a high parameter count (418.6M), massive MACs (18.329 G), and is considerably slower in inference (83.5 ms per batch of size 1) compared to other SOTA unimodal foundation models (e.g., VisionTS: 7.4 ms, MOIRAI: 51.0 ms). This could limit its deployment in real-time or resource-constrained environments.

The paper lacks a direct analysis of performance when text is omitted. Since random masking is used during pretraining to handle unimodal scenarios, it would be beneficial to see a side-by-side comparison on TimeMMD with and without text to explicitly quantify the gain of the synthetic text modality.

There are several typos throughout the manuscript, such as 'Corss-domain' (Page 1), 'corrsponding' (Page 1), 'hevay' (Page 2), 'pionnering' (Page 2), 'merticulously' (multiple pages), 'propriate' (Page 6), and 'scability' (Page 9, 10).

strengths: The paper pioneers a multimodal foundation model paradigm for time series forecasting, effectively combining textual domain knowledge, visual/geometric patterns (endogenous images), and temporal data.

The introduction of Prototype-Guided Flow Matching is a novel and clever idea. Starting the generative flow matching process from retrieved structural prototypes (period/trend) rather than standard Gaussian noise provides an intuitive and effective prior for probabilistic forecasting.

The evaluation is very extensive, spanning multimodal benchmarks (TimeMMD), unimodal deterministic benchmarks (TSFM-Bench), and unimodal probabilistic benchmarks (ProbTS). The model shows state-of-the-art results in both zero-shot and few-shot settings.
The manuscript is well-written, with clear explanations of the architectural modules, detailed appendixes, and useful ablation studies.
weaknesses: Lack of fine-grained modality ablation: There is no ablation study showing the individual performance contributions of the text modality versus the endogenous image modality. Given that rendering 1D time series to 2D/3D images and processing them via a ViT introduces massive computational overhead, it is crucial to know if the image modality provides significant improvements over just using 1D time series and text.

Potential target/future leakage in text generation: In Figure 7, the GPT-4 prompt asks to 'analyze the future trend and characteristics' of the time series, and the generated text describes 'a significant decline and a continuous downward trend'. If such text descriptions are used during inference, they might act as a cheat-sheet containing information about the future horizon. The authors should clarify if the text descriptions used during testing contain any information derived from the ground-truth future horizon.

Real-world text availability and inference protocol: In practical deployment and zero-shot scenarios (such as on TSFM-Bench and ProbTS where text is absent), how is the inference performed? When text is masked/absent, how does the PrototypeRetriever (Eq. 24) compute the prototype weights without the text embedding? Clarifying the exact behavior under unimodal settings is necessary.

High computational cost: As shown in the efficiency analysis (Table 8), Aurora is computationally heavy (418.6M parameters, 18.329 G MACs, and 83.5 ms inference time). This high latency and compute footprint could limit its utility in real-time or resource-constrained applications.

strengths: Pioneering exploration of multimodal time series foundation models, integrating text, rendered images, and time series data to enable cross-domain zero-shot forecasting.

Novel architecture design, featuring token distillation for multimodal compression, a Modality-Guided Self-Attention mechanism to adjust temporal attention based on domain knowledge, and a Prototype-Guided Flow Matching decoder.
The use of a Prototype Bank to provide meaningful trend and periodic starting points instead of pure Gaussian noise is intuitive and theoretically sound for flow matching.

Extensive and rigorous experimental evaluation across 5 popular benchmarks (TimeMMD, TSFM-Bench, ProbTS, TFB, and EPF) in both deterministic/probabilistic and zero-shot/few-shot settings, demonstrating clear state-of-the-art performance.
weaknesses: The textual descriptions used for pretraining are synthesized using GPT-4 based on the raw time series. This heuristic approach, while practical, might introduce artificial patterns or potential data leakage if the LLM's knowledge base already contains similar domain characteristics.

The rendering of 1D time series into 2D 'endogenous images' is fundamentally a transformation of the raw time series rather than a truly independent exogenous modality, which makes the claim of 'image modality' slightly overstated.

High computational complexity and inference latency: As shown in the efficiency analysis (Table 9), Aurora has an inference time of 83.5 ms, which is significantly slower than other foundation models like VisionTS (7.4 ms) and Time-MoE (31.4 ms). The model also requires substantial training resource (30 days on 8 A800 GPUs).
Minor typographical errors exist throughout the paper (e.g., 'Corss-domain' in the Abstract, 'merticulously-designed' on page 1, and 'pionnering' on page 2).

strengths: Well-designed framework that elegantly combines text (domain knowledge), rendered images (capturing geometric/periodic structures), and raw 1D time series into a unified multimodal time series foundation model.

The proposed Prototype-Guided Flow Matching is technically sound and novel; initializing the starting points of flow matching with retrieved trend/period prototypes instead of standard Gaussian noise is a clever way to ease the generation process.
Exceptionally comprehensive experimental validation on 5 major benchmarks (TimeMMD, TSFM-Bench, ProbTS, TFB, EPF) covering zero-shot, few-shot, deterministic, and probabilistic settings.
Very thorough ablation studies and qualitative analyses (such as prototype visualizations and attention maps) that clearly demonstrate the indispensability of each component.
weaknesses: High computational cost: The pre-training phase requires 30 days of training on 8 NVIDIA A800 GPUs, which limits reproducibility and accessibility for researchers with standard budgets.

Inference latency: The parameter count (210.8M) and FLOPs/MACs (18.3 G) are relatively high compared to unimodal foundation models, potentially hindering deployment in resource-constrained or real-time scenarios.

Dependency on text modality: High-quality sample-wise textual descriptions are crucial for optimal performance. While a unimodal mode is supported through masking, executing the full multimodal pipeline requires generating descriptions, often necessitating external LLM APIs (like GPT-4) during downstream inference.
Presence of multiple minor typos throughout the paper (e.g., 'Corss-domain', 'corrsponding', 'retreive', 'inituitively', 'magnitutdes', 'distller') that require careful proofreading.

strengths: Explores the integration of multimodal data (text and vision) into time series foundation models, which is a timely and interesting direction.
Presents a comprehensive model pipeline combining pretrained BERT, ViT, and a generative Flow Matching decoder.
Provides extensive experimental evaluations on multiple well-known time-series benchmarks, along with a detailed appendix containing visualizations.
weaknesses: Potential Future Information Leakage: The text generation process described in Figure 8 and Appendix A.1 uses prompts that ask GPT-4 to 'analyze the future trend and characteristics of this time series'. The generated texts (which are fed as inputs to the model) explicitly describe future behaviors (e.g., 'the future trend might show a slow upward recovery' or 'the electricity consumption is expected to continue to decrease gradually'). Using these text descriptions as input during inference represents a serious future-label leakage and makes the comparison with unimodal baselines highly unfair, as real-world scenarios do not have access to future trend descriptions.

Inherent Inefficiency of Endogenous Images: Converting a 1D time series into a 2D image using FFT period rendering and then encoding it with a Vision Transformer (ViT) is computationally heavy and redundant. Capturing periodic patterns can be done much more efficiently with 1D multi-scale operations. As shown in Table 9, this visual rendering approach leads to massive computational overhead (18.329 G MACs) and slow inference (over 11x slower than VisionTS).

Highly Anomalous Citation Patterns: The manuscript relies heavily on a remarkably large number of citations from '2025' and even '2026' (e.g., multiple 2025/2026 preprints by Wu, Liu, Li, and Qiu). This extreme concentration of future-dated, non-peer-reviewed citations undermines the scholarly foundations of the work.

Incomplete Manuscript: The 'REPRODUCIBILITY STATEMENT' contains unfinished sentences and missing links, leaving blank placeholders: 'We have released our model code and checkpoints on   and   .' This indicates a lack of careful review before submission.
